title: New Orleans joins other cities testing AI 911 operators
excerpt: More and more cities are leaning on AI to help emergency operators.
content_html:
New Orleans, home to more than 300,000 residents and an emergency system that handles thousands of calls each day, is turning to AI for help.

The city recently confirmed that emergency services, overseen by the Orleans Parish Communication District, are deploying an AI triage tool to screen and sort incoming calls to assist human operators. City representatives explained the technology is intended to reduce the number of repetitive calls and prevent lines from bottlenecking.

Basically, if a resident calls in an incident that's already been reported, like a car crash, the AI dispatcher is supposed to handle it.

You May Also Like

The tool, referred to as AI Emergency Call Triage, was developed by AI emergency services company Carbyne. It's still undergoing real-world testing by operators, according to reporting by the Shreveport Times, but has been involved in triaging traffic-related emergency calls since at least 2023. The city also introduced an AI tool for its 311 non-emergency services in April.

Mashable Light Speed

New Orleans is one of several cities introducing AI into emergency and non-emergency call operations, and Carbyne is already working with public safety agencies across the country.

In 2024, the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) published a fact sheet exploring the implementation of AI into emergency service operations, including testimony from early adopters like the Orleans Parish Communication District. The agency determined AI could assist in "automating initial detection and triage, streamlining call flow," and reducing call load for human operators. The NTIA's fact sheet argued AI would be most efficient when deployed for translation, triage, automatic callback systems, and geofencing.

Carbyne has multiple partnerships with transportation and law enforcement authorities around the country, including a recent partnership with Washington, D.C. city services to modernize public safety systems like 911 call handling.

In June, reporting from the Seattle Times revealed that the Seattle Fire Department had been deploying an AI-powered triage tool similar to Carbyne's product for nearly two years. The tool in question, developed by Denmark-based company Corti, monitored live medical calls and advised operators on where and when to dispatch immediate services. Corti's AI was also deployed by Boston Emergency Medical Services, according to the company.

Critics of such generative AI products have repeatedly raised concerns about caller data privacy, the potential for AI model bias when interacting with diverse populations of callers, and the limitations of AI-generated voice tools in general. Many have taken issue with the lack of transparency by city services integrating AI into public-facing call lines without explicit notice.

content_html_zh:
新奥尔良拥有超过 30 万居民，其应急系统每天处理数千个电话，该市正在向人工智能寻求帮助。

该市最近证实，由奥尔良教区通信区监督的紧急服务部门正在部署人工智能分类工具来筛选和分类来电，以协助人工接线员。 市代表解释说，该技术旨在减少重复呼叫的次数并防止线路出现瓶颈。

基本上，如果居民致电已经报告的事件，例如车祸，人工智能调度员应该处理它。

你可能也喜欢

该工具被称为“AI紧急呼叫分类”，由AI紧急服务公司Carbyne开发。 据《什里夫波特时报》报道，它仍在接受运营商的实际测试，但至少从 2023 年起就开始参与与交通相关的紧急呼叫的分类。 该市还在 4 月份为其 311 非紧急服务引入了人工智能工具。

可混搭光速

新奥尔良是将人工智能引入紧急和非紧急呼叫操作的几个城市之一，Carbyne 已经与全国各地的公共安全机构合作。

2024 年，国家电信和信息管理局 (NTIA) 发布了一份情况说明书，探讨将人工智能应用于紧急服务运营，其中包括奥尔良教区通信区等早期采用者的证词。 该机构确定人工智能可以帮助“自动执行初始检测和分类、简化呼叫流程”并减少人工接线员的呼叫负载。 NTIA 的情况说明书认为，将人工智能部署用于翻译、分类、自动回拨系统和地理围栏时，效率最高。

Carbyne 与全国各地的交通和执法机构建立了多种合作伙伴关系，包括最近与华盛顿特区的合作伙伴关系。 公共安全系统现代化的城市服务，例如 911 呼叫处理。

6 月，《西雅图时报》报道称，西雅图消防局近两年来一直在部署类似于 Carbyne 产品的人工智能分类工具。 该工具由总部位于丹麦的 Corti 公司开发，可以监控实时医疗呼叫，并建议操作员在何时何地派遣即时服务。 据该公司称，Corti 的人工智能也被波士顿紧急医疗服务中心部署。

对此类生成式人工智能产品的批评者多次提出了对呼叫者数据隐私、与不同呼叫者群体交互时人工智能模型偏差的可能性以及人工智能生成的语音工具总体局限性的担忧。 许多人对城市服务在没有明确通知的情况下将人工智能集成到面向公众的呼叫线路中缺乏透明度的问题提出了质疑。
